key_insight: MedHiVE models anatomical hierarchies in both 3D scans and reports to learn locally detailed and globally contextualized vision-language representations.
clinical_relevance: Anatomy-aware representations could support medical-image segmentation, classification, and detection, though clinical utility is not established by the abstract.
method: Routes image and text tokens through a local Soft Mixture-of-Experts layer.
Fuses local features through a global Soft Mixture-of-Experts layer.
Uses contrastive learning to align anatomy-level and whole-scan vision-language representations.
evidence_signal: Pre-trained on over 25,000 CT scans with anatomical supervision, MedHiVE reportedly outperformed 11 state-of-the-art methods across 6 datasets covering segmentation, classification, and detection.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish prospective clinical performance or robustness across institutions and scanning protocols.
paper_title: Multimodal Hierarchical Mixture-of-Experts for 3D Medical Vision-Language Modeling
